To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have designed and implemented a novel position histogram encoding that is effective at capturing the distribution of elements in XML documents; (2) we have developed an efficient algorithm to estimate query results sizes by combining position histograms using a pH-join operation that can be applied to any query pattern; and (3) we have extended our technique to exploit the no-overlap property of XML data to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the estimation algorithm.
We propose a novel histogram encoding for position information that enables accurate and efficient estimation of the size of complex queries, and of intermediate query plans, for XML.
we propose a novel histogram encoding for XML element position, which allows us to estimate query results with high accuracy, and at low cost.

our technique is able to estimate the number of elements that match the query pattern with high precision (less than 5% error) in less than 1 microsecond on an average query, using a small amount of space (less than 1% of the size of the database) and with a very small overhead on query processing (less than 0.1% increase in query execution time).
our technique provides an effective solution to the problem of query result size estimation in XML, and is a significant contribution to the area of query optimization for XML.

the techniques presented in this paper are effective and efficient for estimating the size of query result sets in native XML databases, and can be used for effective query optimization and for user guidance.

the use of position histograms can be a powerful tool for query optimization in XML, and that the use of coverage histograms can further improve performance.
